title: Derived internal Hom commutes with restriction to opens
statement: Let $(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be a ringed space [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism], let $K,L$ be objects of the derived category $D(\mathcal O_X)$ of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and let $U\subseteq X$ be open, with restrictions $K|_U,L|_U\in D(\mathcal O_U)$ computed termwise on representing complexes. Then there is a canonical isomorphism $R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_U}(K|_U,L|_U)\cong R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(K,L)|_U$ in $D(\mathcal O_U)$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom].

proof.text: Represent $L$ by a complex $\mathcal L^\bullet$ and choose a functorial K-injective resolution $\mathcal L^\bullet\to I^\bullet$ in the category of $\mathcal O_X$-modules. By the definition of derived internal Hom, $R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(K,L)$ is represented by the sheaf Hom complex $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(K^\bullet,I^\bullet)$ for any representative $K^\bullet$ of $K$.

By the open-restriction K-injective lemma [lem-sc-derived-k-injective-restrict-open], $j^{-1}I^\bullet$ is K-injective on $U$. Restriction to an open is exact (the cohomology sheaves of $j^{-1}$ of a complex are the restrictions of its cohomology sheaves, as sections and stalks over opens of $U$ are unchanged), so $j^{-1}\mathcal L^\bullet\to j^{-1}I^\bullet$ is still a quasi-isomorphism and hence a K-injective resolution of $L|_U$. It therefore represents the restriction $L|_U$ and, by the definition of derived internal Hom, computes $R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_U}(K|_U,L|_U)$.

For each open $V\subseteq U$, the definition of sheaf Hom gives $\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(A,B)(V)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_V}(A|_V,B|_V)=\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_U}(A|_U,B|_U)(V)$. These equalities commute with restriction maps. In degree $n$, the Hom complex is the product over $p\in\mathbf Z$ of these Hom sheaves; products of sheaves of modules are computed sectionwise, so restriction identifies that product with the product on $U$. The differential $d(f)^p=d_I^{p+n}\circ f^p-(-1)^n f^{p+1}\circ d_K^p$ is unchanged on $V$. Thus $j^{-1}\mathcal Hom^\bullet(K^\bullet,I^\bullet)\cong\mathcal Hom^\bullet(j^{-1}K^\bullet,j^{-1}I^\bullet)$ as complexes.

By Steps 1 and 2, its source and target represent $R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(K,L)|_U$ and $R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_U}(K|_U,L|_U)$ respectively. Each component is restriction of a local module map; hence it is natural in both arguments and in successive open inclusions. Independence of the chosen representatives and K-injective resolution follows from the canonical independence clause of the derived internal Hom definition.
